claims.text: Heat treatment of AlCrFeCoNi at 800°C for 2 hours will form a homogeneous solid solution.
The heat-treated homogeneous solid solution will improve the radiation tolerance of AlCrFeCoNi.
The intervention will preserve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeCoNi under irradiation.
A homogeneous solid solution will reduce the accumulation of radiation damage.
The homogeneous solid solution eliminates heterogeneous interfaces.
Heterogeneous interfaces can act as sinks for radiation-induced defects.
Eliminating heterogeneous defect-sink interfaces will reduce radiation-damage accumulation.
The heat-treated alloy will show a 10% improvement in yield strength relative to unmodified AlCrFeCoNi.
The heat-treated alloy will show a 20% reduction in swelling relative to unmodified AlCrFeCoNi.
The predicted effect will hold during irradiation with 2 MeV protons at 300°C to 5 dpa.

contradictions.description: The mechanism identifies heterogeneous interfaces as sinks for radiation-induced defects but then claims that eliminating those sinks will reduce defect accumulation. As written, the proposed causal direction is internally incoherent unless an additional harmful role of those interfaces is specified.
